transcript.text: Thanks, Maya and Lina. Let me lay out how I'd structure the onboarding within the three-day schedule. The Research Operations role is well-suited to a reduced schedule because the core tasks — coordinating research workflows, managing documentation, and supporting project tracking — can be organized around focused working blocks rather than requiring daily presence. For the eight-week onboarding period with Sofia, I'd propose the following: Sofia and Lina would have two structured check-in sessions per week on Lina's available working days — one at the start of the week to review priorities and assignments, and one mid-week to review progress and address questions. Since Lina can't attend recurring Friday meetings, we'll make sure any team-wide Research meetings that Lina needs to participate in are scheduled on her available days, and we'll use asynchronous updates for anything that falls on Fridays. The eight-week buddy period should give Lina enough runway to get up to speed on Research Operations processes even at three days per week, since Sofia will be available for guidance throughout. I'd also suggest we front-load the first two weeks with more intensive onboarding tasks — system access setup, process walkthroughs, and shadowing sessions — so that by weeks three through eight, Lina is gradually taking on more independent work. One thing I want to flag: we'll need to make sure the two handoff sessions Owen mentioned are scheduled early in the transition, ideally in week one, so they don't overlap with the onboarding intensity. Does that structure work for everyone, and are there any adjustments we should make before Maya records the final terms?
